F1.name: best_responses
F1.interpretation: Each curve gives one firm's optimal price for a fixed rival price. Their intersection is the unique pure-strategy Nash equilibrium. In this scenario Lyft has the larger demand intercept and charges the higher equilibrium price.
F1.scope: Illustrative model parameters. Prices are in model units. No parameters were fitted to TLC data.

F2.name: symmetric_price_and_profit
F2.interpretation: Both firms choose the same price and earn the same profit. As relative-price sensitivity rises, price and profit fall. Profit has zero slope at s = 0.
F2.scope: Only s varies. Prices and profits are in illustrative model units.

F3.name: asymmetric_prices_and_shares
F3.interpretation: Lyft has the larger demand intercept and charges the higher price throughout. As relative-price sensitivity increases, the price gap and the share gap narrow. Uber gains share throughout, although its own price initially rises.
F3.scope: Only s varies. Shares are percentages of modelled duopoly demand. Parameters are illustrative.
